overview.description: Labrador Retrievers are America's most popular dog breed, known for their friendly, active, and outgoing personalities. However, they possess a genetic predisposition to obesity due to a mutation in the POMC gene, which affects their regulation of appetite and satiety.
overview.metabolicTrait: High genetic predisposition to constant hunger (lack of natural feeling of fullness).

puppy.calciumPhosphorusRatio: 1.2:1 to 1.5:1 (critical for controlled large-breed bone growth)
puppy.feedingFrequency: 3 to 4 meals per day until 6 months, then 2 meals.

adult.fatPercentage: 10% - 14% (lower fat for neutered/spayed or less active adults)
adult.caloriesPerDay: 1200 - 1600 kcal (depending on activity level and weight, e.g., ~30 kcal per lb for moderately active adults)
adult.feedingFrequency: 2 meals per day to prevent gorging and reduce bloat risk.

senior.proteinPercentage: 20% - 26% (high quality, highly digestible to maintain muscle mass)
senior.fatPercentage: 8% - 12% (reduced calories to prevent weight gain in lower activity)
senior.specialAdditions: Glucosamine, Chondroitin, Omega-3 Fatty Acids (EPA/DHA), L-Carnitine.

items.name: Carrots
items.benefits: Low calorie, high in beta-carotene and fiber; great for dental health when raw.
items.servingTip: Wash thoroughly and cut into bite-sized pieces to prevent choking.

items.name: Green Beans
items.benefits: Extremely low in calorie and highly filling (ideal for weight-loss diets for hungry Labs).
items.servingTip: Fresh, steamed, or plain canned (no added salt/sodium).

items.name: Pumpkin
items.benefits: Pure canned pumpkin is excellent for digestive health, firming stools, and providing soluble fiber.
items.servingTip: Use 100% pure pumpkin puree, NOT pumpkin pie mix with spices and sugar.

items.name: Sweet Potatoes
items.benefits: Rich in dietary fiber, vitamins A, B6, and C.
items.servingTip: Must be cooked thoroughly (baked or boiled) and served plain without butter or skin.

items.name: Cucumbers
items.benefits: Low calorie, high water content, excellent hydrating snack for summer.
items.servingTip: Slice into rounds; peel if desired.

items.name: Zucchini
items.benefits: Safe, low calorie, contains vitamins C and K.

items.name: Blueberries
items.benefits: Powerhouse of antioxidants, vitamins C and K, and fiber.
items.servingTip: Fresh or frozen as a crunchy treat.

items.name: Apples
items.benefits: Good source of vitamins A and C, and dietary fiber.
items.servingTip: Remove core and seeds entirely (cyanide risk in seeds); slice into wedges.

items.name: Watermelon
items.benefits: Hydrating, rich in lycopene and vitamins A and C.
items.servingTip: Remove rind and all black seeds completely.

items.name: Bananas
items.benefits: High in potassium, vitamins, biotin, and fiber.
items.servingTip: Give in moderation due to high natural sugar content.

items.name: Strawberries
items.benefits: Contain fiber, vitamin C, and an enzyme that can help whiten teeth.
items.servingTip: Remove stems and wash thoroughly; cut in half for smaller dogs.

items.name: Chicken Breast
items.benefits: Lean source of essential amino acids and protein.
items.servingTip: Must be boiled or baked completely plain, boneless, and skinless (no seasonings, onions, or garlic).

items.name: Turkey
items.servingTip: Plain, lean, fully cooked, no skin and no bones.

items.name: Eggs
items.benefits: Complete protein source packed with fatty acids and vitamins.
items.servingTip: Cooked thoroughly (scrambled or boiled) without oil, butter, or salt. Avoid raw egg whites regularly due to biotin binding.

items.name: Plain Greek Yogurt
items.benefits: Rich in probiotics and calcium for gut health.
items.servingTip: Unsweetened, plain, low-fat or fat-free. Ensure NO artificial sweeteners like xylitol are present.

items.name: Salmon
items.benefits: Exceptional source of Omega-3 fatty acids for skin, coat, and joint health.
items.servingTip: Must be fully cooked; never feed raw salmon due to fatal salmon poisoning disease.

items.name: Rice (White or Brown)
items.benefits: Easily digestible carbohydrate; great for upset stomachs.
items.servingTip: Plainly boiled without salt or butter.

items.name: Oatmeal
items.benefits: Good source of soluble fiber, beneficial for dogs with digestive issues.
items.servingTip: Cooked with water or plain milk (avoid instant flavored oatmeal packets).

items.name: Quinoa
items.benefits: High protein pseudo-grain, complete amino acid profile.

toxicFoods.name: Chocolate
toxicFoods.symptoms: Vomiting, diarrhea, excessive thirst, rapid heart rate, seizures, heart failure, death.

toxicFoods.name: Grapes and Raisins
toxicFoods.symptoms: Vomiting, lethargy, loss of appetite, abdominal pain, sudden kidney failure and lack of urination.

toxicFoods.name: Onions, Garlic, Chives, and Leeks
toxicFoods.toxin: Organosulfoxides (causes oxidative damage to red blood cells)
toxicFoods.symptoms: Weakness, lethargy, pale gums, elevated heart rate, red/brown urine, hemolytic anemia.

toxicFoods.name: Xylitol (Artificial Sweetener)
toxicFoods.symptoms: Rapid drop in blood sugar (hypoglycemia), vomiting, weakness, staggering, liver failure, seizures within 15-60 minutes.

toxicFoods.name: Macadamia Nuts
toxicFoods.symptoms: Weakness in hind limbs, tremors, elevated body temperature, vomiting, joint stiffness.

toxicFoods.name: Alcohol
toxicFoods.symptoms: Vomiting, diarrhea, central nervous system depression, coordination loss, breathing difficulties, coma.

toxicFoods.name: Avocado
toxicFoods.toxin: Persin (found in fruit, pit, leaves, and bark)
toxicFoods.symptoms: Vomiting, diarrhea, myocardial damage (especially toxic to birds/horses, but pits pose severe choking/obstruction hazard for Labs).

toxicFoods.name: Coffee, Tea, and Caffeine
toxicFoods.symptoms: Restlessness, rapid breathing, heart palpitations, muscle tremors, seizures.

toxicFoods.name: Cooked Bones
toxicFoods.symptoms: Internal lacerations, choking, gastrointestinal perforation, severe bowel obstruction.

toxicFoods.name: Yeast Dough
toxicFoods.toxin: Ethanol production and gas expansion in stomach
toxicFoods.symptoms: Severe abdominal bloating (GDV risk), staggering, disorientation, alcohol poisoning.

weightManagement: Use slow-feeder bowls or puzzle toys to slow down voracious eaters.
Substitute up to 10-20% of regular kibble with steamed green beans or pumpkin for a filling, low-calorie meal volume.
Strictly measure meals using a measuring cup rather than free-feeding.
Monitor body condition score (BCS) regularly: Labs should have a clear waistline when viewed from above and a tuck-up at the abdomen.
gdvPrevention: Avoid strenuous exercise 1 hour before and 1 hour after meals.
Split daily food into two separate meals.
Prevent rapid gulping of food and water.

recommendedSupplements.name: Glucosamine and Chondroitin Sulfate
recommendedSupplements.purpose: Supports joint cartilage health, cushioning, and mobility, crucial for large breeds prone to hip dysplasia.

recommendedSupplements.name: Omega-3 Fatty Acids (Fish Oil - EPA/DHA)
recommendedSupplements.purpose: Reduces systemic inflammation, supports cardiovascular health, promotes a shiny double coat, and aids cognitive function.

recommendedSupplements.name: Probiotics & Prebiotics
recommendedSupplements.purpose: Enhances gut microbiome balance, improves nutrient absorption, and boosts immune response.

recommendedSupplements.name: L-Carnitine
recommendedSupplements.purpose: Supports fat metabolism and lean muscle maintenance in weight-management diets.
